werk/radiohead-kid-a.text:
After the success of OK Computer, Radiohead were exhausted. Singer Thom Yorke was struggling with writer's block, listened almost exclusively to electronic music from the label Warp, and wanted more rhythm and less melody. From January 1999 the band worked with producer Nigel Godrich in Paris, Copenhagen, Gloucestershire and a new studio in Oxfordshire. The sessions were difficult. The group even agreed to split up if no album came out of them.

The result sounds unlike anything that came before: synthesizers, the ondes Martenot, guitars drenched in effects, and abstract lyrics that Yorke assembled from loose phrases. No singles were released. Many listeners found the new sound pretentious or needlessly bleak. Later, Rolling Stone, Pitchfork and The Times nevertheless named Kid A the best album of the 2000s.
werk/radiohead-kid-a.listen: Listen to Everything In Its Right Place, the first song Yorke wrote for this album, on his piano. Notice how the voice among the electronic sounds works more like an instrument than a lead vocal line.

werk/radiohead-ok-computer.text:
After the tour for The Bends, the band did not want to make another introspective album. Radiohead recorded the album in 1996 and early 1997, in a converted barn near Didcot in Oxfordshire and at the country house St Catherine's Court near Bath. Nigel Godrich, with whom the group had recorded the charity song Lucky in five hours in 1995, grew into a co-producer. The strings were recorded at Abbey Road Studios.

The lyrics deal with consumerism, alienation, technological anxiety and paranoia. The sound is densely layered, with natural reverb and few overdubs. Paranoid Android, Karma Police, Lucky and No Surprises were released as singles. The label EMI expected little of the record, but it received a great deal of praise, won a Grammy for Best Alternative Music Album and helped steer British rock away from Britpop. In 2014 the Library of Congress added the album to the National Recording Registry.
werk/radiohead-ok-computer.listen: Listen to Lucky, the song that was recorded in just five hours in 1995. According to Yorke it was the first mark on the wall for this album: notice the atmosphere, which already points ahead to the rest of the record.

werk/radiohead-pablo-honey.text:
Radiohead recorded their debut album in 1992 at Chipping Norton Recording Studios in Oxfordshire, in three weeks. The managers wanted to conquer the American market and therefore chose the American producers Sean Slade and Paul Q. Kolderie. The band had little studio experience and wanted to squeeze every idea from twenty years of listening into a single record. Guitars were layered several times over one another to create a thick wall of sound. The title comes from a prank call by the Jerky Boys.

The song Creep began as an afterthought, until the producers heard it. It has a quiet verse and a loud chorus with bursts of guitar noise. At first the single made little impression, but via radio in Israel and America it grew into a hit, and in 1993 it reached number 7 in Britain. Reviewers were generally positive, although some found the album unfinished. The band members themselves are critical of it.
werk/radiohead-pablo-honey.listen: Listen to Creep and notice the difference between the quiet verse and the loud chorus. Hear how the guitar breaks loose in bursts in the chorus.

werk/radiohead-the-bends.text:
After the hit Creep, Radiohead felt a great deal of pressure, and singer Thom Yorke fell ill after the world tour. Even so, he went on to write new songs that guitarist Ed O'Brien thought much better than the debut Pablo Honey. The band chose John Leckie as producer. Recording began in February 1994 at RAK Studios in London and progressed slowly, with pressure from the label. It was the first album with Nigel Godrich and the artist Stanley Donwood. The three guitarists were now given separate roles.

The Bends was released on 13 March 1995 on Parlophone and combines guitar songs and ballads, with more restrained arrangements and more cryptic lyrics than the debut. Singles included My Iron Lung, Fake Plastic Trees, Just and Street Spirit (Fade Out), the band's first top-five hit in England. The album reached number four in the British chart and made the band more than a one-hit wonder. It influenced later bands such as Coldplay, Muse and Travis.
werk/radiohead-the-bends.listen: Listen to Street Spirit (Fade Out) and notice the subdued mood and Thom Yorke's singing. Hear how this song fits the quieter side of the album.

werk/radiohead-the-king-of-limbs.text:
After In Rainbows in 2007, Radiohead looked for less conventional song structures and recording methods. From May 2009 to January 2011 the band worked on the album with producer Nigel Godrich, including three weeks at Drew Barrymore's house in Los Angeles. An experiment with turntables and software instead of conventional instruments ended up lasting six months. Much of the material arose from looping and manipulating the band's playing. Thom Yorke wrote melodies and lyrics over it. The title refers to an ancient oak in Savernake Forest.

The sound is rhythmic and electronic, with a great deal of sampling, looping and natural sounds. The album was released on 18 February 2011 as a download, with no singles. For Lotus Flower, however, the band did make a video in which Yorke dances. It divided listeners because of its unusual production and its short running time, but Rolling Stone and NME counted it among the best records of the year.
werk/radiohead-the-king-of-limbs.listen: Listen to Bloom and notice the rhythmic layers sliding over one another.

werk/rage-against-the-machine-rage-again.text:
The debut was released on 6 November 1992 on Epic Records and rests largely on the group's first demo tape, completed eleven months earlier. Seven of the ten songs were already on that tape. The cover shows the photograph of the Vietnamese monk Thích Quảng Đức, who burned himself to death in 1963. All the songs carry a political message. The sleeve notes state that no samples, keyboards or synthesizers were used.

The sound blends driving rock with mostly rapped vocals. Zack de la Rocha shares the spotlight with guitarist Tom Morello, who combines metal, blues rock and jazz and sometimes imitates the sound of a scratching DJ. Critics praised the convincing vocals and the political intent. One reviewer called it the first album to bring rap and heavy metal together successfully. Know Your Enemy and Wake Up were singled out as highlights. Rolling Stone ranks the album among the best metal records of all time.
werk/rage-against-the-machine-rage-again.listen: Listen to Know Your Enemy and notice how the rapped vocals and the guitar keep giving each other room.

werk/rage-against-the-machine-the-battle.text:
This third studio album was released on 2 November 1999 on Epic Records and was Rage Against the Machine's last album of original songs before the band split up in 2000. The music is described as rap metal and funk metal. The cover is an original piece of graffiti art by the Los Angeles street artist Joey Krebs.

The songs are politically charged. Voice of the Voiceless is about the activist and journalist Mumia Abu-Jamal and refers to a letter by Mao Zedong. For Testify and Sleep Now in the Fire, the documentary maker Michael Moore directed the videos, in which he appears himself. The album went straight to number 1 on the American Billboard 200. Guerrilla Radio won a Grammy for Best Hard Rock Performance, and both Time and Rolling Stone declared the record the best album of 1999.
werk/rage-against-the-machine-the-battle.listen: Listen to Guerrilla Radio and notice how the vocals and the rhythm section together lay down a tight, hard groove. This is the song that won a Grammy.

werk/ralph-towner-batik.text:
Ralph Towner recorded Batik in January 1978 and released it on ECM in September of that year. The album is a trio recording: Towner plays twelve-string guitar, classical guitar and piano, with Eddie Gómez on bass and Jack DeJohnette on drums. He wrote all five pieces himself.

The longest composition is the title track, which lasts well over sixteen minutes. According to the reviewer Scott Yanow of AllMusic, the music unfolds slowly but logically. Towner's sound is quiet, but there is a great deal of inner heat in it. Yanow considers the album worth listening to closely, at high volume.
werk/ralph-towner-batik.listen: In Batik, listen to how guitar, bass and drums give each other room as the piece develops over more than sixteen minutes. Notice what changes and what stays the same.

werk/ralph-towner-diary.text:
Diary is the first solo album by the American jazz guitarist and composer Ralph Towner. He recorded it in two days in April 1973 and released it that same year on ECM.

Towner plays not only twelve-string and classical guitar here, but also piano and gong. By layering recordings on top of one another he accompanies himself, so that it sounds as if more musicians are playing. The result is an intimate, chamber-like sound. The AllMusic reviewer thought of it as a solo performance with an extra layer, and heard in the method of working something of Bill Evans's Conversations with Myself. He gave the album three stars.
werk/ralph-towner-diary.listen: Listen to Entry In A Diary and try to hear which instruments are sounding together. Notice how the guitar and the piano complement each other, even though it is a single player.

werk/ralph-towner-trios-solos.text:
Trios / Solos was made in two days in November 1972 and released in June 1973 on ECM. Manfred Eicher produced it. Guitarist Ralph Towner plays here together with bassist Glen Moore. Tabla player Collin Walcott and oboist Paul McCandless take part as guests.

Towner plays twelve-string guitar, classical guitar and piano. The title says what you hear: changing line-ups, from solo pieces to trios with bass and an additional instrument. In this way the guitar, the bass, the tabla and the oboe sound different together every time. The AllMusic reviewer gave the album four stars. He found some pieces a little aimless, but praised the way the four sounds touch and inspire one another.
werk/ralph-towner-trios-solos.listen: Listen to Brujo, where the tabla joins in, and notice how that percussion relates to the guitar. Can you hear who takes the lead, or do they flow into one another?

werk/ramin-djawadi-medal-of-honor-warfig.text:
This soundtrack belongs to the 2012 first-person shooter Medal of Honor: Warfighter. Ramin Djawadi wrote the music, as he did for the previous instalment, Medal of Honor in 2010. Themes from that first game return, sometimes in a slightly different form. The album has 21 tracks, two of which are by Mike Shinoda, the co-vocalist and rapper of Linkin Park. It was released on 25 September 2012 via iTunes and Amazon, almost a month before the game.

The theme song is Castle of Glass by Linkin Park, with variations on the soundtrack. According to Loudwire, the song has striking electronic elements and a melody reminiscent of country music. The song also served as a promotional single and was nominated for Best Song in a Game at the 2012 Spike Video Game Awards.
werk/ramin-djawadi-medal-of-honor-warfig.listen: Listen to Lena's Theme and notice how the music sets a mood, just as you would expect from game music.

werk/ramones-ramones.text:
The debut of this New York punk band came about after Hit Parader editor Lisa Robinson saw them play in 1975 and started writing about them. She asked Danny Fields to become their manager, and producer Craig Leon managed to persuade Sire president Seymour Stein. In January 1976 they recorded the album at Plaza Sound, in a week and for 6,400 dollars. Three days for the instruments and four for the vocals were enough.

The songs are short and lightning fast: many of them go well above 160 beats per minute, and the longest lasts two and a half minutes. The record opens with Blitzkrieg Bop. The lyrics deal with violence, drugs, relationships, humour and Nazism. Commercially the record was not a success, but the reviews were glowing. The songs later came to be regarded as one of the most influential punk records, with an influence on grunge and heavy metal.
werk/ramones-ramones.listen: Listen to Blitzkrieg Bop and notice how short and tight the song is: a straightforward tempo with no detours.

werk/ramones-rocket-to-russia.text:
In the summer of 1977 punk was at its peak: the first groups from the New York underground were getting record deals. The Ramones then released Sheena Is a Punk Rocker. Sire gave the band between 25,000 and 30,000 dollars, far more than before, and that money went mainly into the production. Recording began on 21 August at Mediasound Studios in Manhattan, a former church. Usually the first take was used. Johnny Ramone wanted to sound better than the Sex Pistols.

The sound has more surf rock than before, many songs are short and simply built, and almost all the lyrics are funny. It was the last record with drummer Tommy Ramone. Critics appreciated the more mature production. Sales were disappointing: the album got no further than number 49 on the Billboard 200.
werk/ramones-rocket-to-russia.listen: Listen to Sheena Is a Punk Rocker and notice how short and straightforward the song is, with a surf-rock sound.

werk/ramsey-lewis-goin-latin.text:
Goin' Latin is a studio album by pianist Ramsey Lewis featuring Latin American percussion and styles. Cadet Records released it in 1967. The record reached number 2 on the Billboard Jazz Albums chart and number 16 on the Billboard Soul Albums chart.

The programme includes Hey, Mrs. Jones, Summer Samba, Lara's Theme from Doctor Zhivago and Cast Your Fate to the Wind by Vince Guaraldi, alongside original pieces by the arranger Richard Evans such as Blue Bongo. Thom Jurek of AllMusic praised Evans's arrangements and the soulful, bass-heavy sound. In his view this suits the album's fondness for bossa nova, discotheque boogaloo and a light form of Latin soul.
werk/ramsey-lewis-goin-latin.listen: In Summer Samba, listen to the piano and notice how the Latin percussion colours the rhythm.

werk/ramsey-lewis-the-movie-album.text:
The Movie Album was released in June 1967 on Cadet Records. Esmond Edwards produced the record, which was recorded in 1966. Ramsey Lewis plays piano, with Cleveland Eaton on bass and Maurice White on drums. An orchestra and choir conducted by Richard Evans supplement the trio. The album contains theme music from various feature films.

Among the tracks are Theme from The Pawnbroker by Quincy Jones, From Russia with Love, The Shadow of Your Smile and The Gentle Rain. Evans himself wrote Saturday Night After the Movies and Goin' Hollywood. The record reached number 5 on the Billboard chart of best-selling jazz albums. AllMusic gave it two out of five stars.
werk/ramsey-lewis-the-movie-album.listen: In The Shadow of Your Smile, listen to the piano and notice how the familiar film melody is played by the trio.

werk/ramsey-lewis-wade-in-the-water.text:
Ramsey Lewis released this album in 1966 on Cadet Records. It followed The In Crowd, and according to one reviewer this record, too, unmistakably evokes the time in which it was made. Lewis plays keyboards, Cleveland Eaton bass and Maurice White drums. Richard Evans wrote the arrangements and conducted. Bob Kidder and Bruce Swedien recorded the record.

The repertoire is a mixture of a traditional, soul numbers such as Ain't That Peculiar and Uptight, a pop song by Burt Bacharach and Hal David and even Day Tripper by The Beatles. The opening track Wade in the Water became a successful single. Hold It Right There won a Grammy Award for Best Rhythm and Blues Performance by a Group, Vocal or Instrumental. The album climbed high in the Billboard charts.
werk/ramsey-lewis-wade-in-the-water.listen: Listen to Day Tripper and notice how a familiar song by The Beatles sounds here as an instrumental jazz piece.

werk/randy-newman-12-songs.text:
12 Songs is the second studio album by the American singer-songwriter Randy Newman and was released in April 1970 on Reprise Records. It sounds like swampy roots music with introspective, satirical lyrics. He left behind the complex orchestrations of his debut and chose an Americana rock line-up, with guitarists such as Ry Cooder, Clarence White and Ron Elliott. The only single was Have You Seen My Baby?. Several songs had already been recorded by others, such as Mama Told Me Not to Come by Eric Burdon.

The record received good reviews straight away. Rolling Stone spoke of the full emergence of an innovator, and Robert Christgau later called it a perfect album. Here he speaks through recognisable American outsiders and touches on themes such as the generation gap, violence, racism and alienation. In 2003 Rolling Stone placed it at number 354 on its list of the greatest albums of all time.
werk/randy-newman-12-songs.listen: Listen to Mama Told Me Not to Come and notice how loosely the band plays and how Newman tells the story in his slow, indifferent voice.

werk/randy-newman-born-again.text:
Born Again is Randy Newman's sixth studio album and was released in August 1979. On the cover he sits in an office with make-up on his face, an obvious parody of Kiss, and dollar signs over his eyes: a joke about the commercialisation of rock music. He wrote and arranged all the songs himself.

Before its release Newman called the record a greater insult than his hit Short People and expected the album to catch on. It did not: sales were disappointing and the reviews were mixed. Later he said he had forgotten that people first need to know who you are. Rolling Stone found the tone snide and nihilistic. The New York Times, by contrast, heard a trace of anger that keeps the songs from sounding cheap. He himself called it the strangest record he ever made.
werk/randy-newman-born-again.listen: Listen to It's Money That I Love and notice how the title immediately points to the theme of the cover: money and commerce.

werk/randy-newman-good-old-boys.text:
Randy Newman first conceived this album as a concept record about Johnny Cutler, an ordinary man from the Deep South. That idea partly survived, but the album became a collection of glimpses of the people of the South in general. As on his previous record, he touches on taboo subjects such as slavery and racism. The opening track Rednecks is a satire on both the institutional racism of the South and the hypocrisy of the North.

He also works in historical events: Louisiana 1927 is about the great Mississippi flood. For Every Man a King, a song by the Louisiana politician Huey Long, he played with members of the Eagles. The album was released in September 1974 and was his first big commercial success, reaching number 36 in the American chart. Robert Christgau gave it an A, and later guides rated it with five stars.
werk/randy-newman-good-old-boys.listen: In Rednecks, listen to the irony of the lyrics and to how Newman sings as a Southerner he is playing.

werk/randy-newman-little-criminals.text:
Little Criminals is the fifth studio album by the American singer-songwriter Randy Newman. Like almost all his work, it leaves the usual pop themes alone: I'll Be Home is the only love song. Newman prefers to tell stories about eccentric characters, with cynical outlooks. He wrote all the songs, conducted and played keyboards, and Michael Boddicker programmed the synthesizers. Members of the Eagles, such as Glenn Frey and Joe Walsh, played and sang along.

Opener Short People became a hit. According to Record World, Baltimore is as serious as Short People was funny. The New York Times considered it Newman's first record with as many musical jokes as verbal ones. The album reached number 8 in the 1977 Pazz & Jop Critics Poll.
werk/randy-newman-little-criminals.listen: Listen to Short People and notice the light-hearted music accompanying a lyric that, according to Newman himself, was purely a joke.

werk/randy-newman-sail-away.text:
Sail Away is Randy Newman's third studio album and was released on 23 May 1972 on Reprise Records. Lenny Waronker and Russ Titelman produced it. He wrote all the songs himself, but some had already been recorded by others, such as Simon Smith and the Amazing Dancing Bear, a British hit for Alan Price in 1967. He re-recorded Last Night I Had a Dream with a clearly different arrangement from the one on his 1968 single. In 2002 Rhino issued a reissue with bonus tracks.

The record has had a lasting influence. Rolling Stone placed it at number 268 among the greatest albums of all time. Brian Wilson said that he played the record over and over in a difficult period. Burn On, about the 1969 fire on the Cuyahoga River, plays over the opening titles of the film Major League, and You Can Leave Your Hat On later became famous in versions by Joe Cocker and Tom Jones.
werk/randy-newman-sail-away.listen: Listen to Burn On and notice the mood of the song, which is about the river in Cleveland that caught fire in 1969.

werk/ravi-shankar-the-sounds-of-india.text:
The Sounds of India is an album by Ravi Shankar that explains Hindustani classical music to a Western audience. It was released in 1957 on Columbia Records and recorded in the label's New York studio, under the direction of George Avakian, the producer of Miles Davis. The model was The Sounds of India by Ali Akbar Khan, in which the musician himself explains what he plays.

For each piece there is a short lesson. He plays sitar, accompanied by Chatur Lal on tabla and N.C. Mullick on tanpura. The album is now regarded as being of historical importance: it shows both his skill and his wish to teach the West. Yoshi Kato calls it an excellent entry point to this music.
werk/ravi-shankar-the-sounds-of-india.listen: In An Introduction to Indian Music, listen to how the music is explained before the actual playing begins.

werk/ravi-shankar-west-meets-east.text:
West Meets East is a joint album by sitar player Ravi Shankar and violinist Yehudi Menuhin, released in 1967. It grew out of their performance in June 1966 at the Bath Festival. Their friendship began in the early 1950s in India, and Menuhin had since done a great deal to make Indian music known in the West. Tabla player Alla Rakha, pianist Hephzibah Menuhin and Prodyot Sen on tanpura also play on the record.

It opens with Prabhati, a composition by Shankar based on Raga Gunakali. Swara Kakali is a reworking of a piece based on Raga Tilang. The whole of the second side is filled with the third violin sonata by the Romanian composer George Enescu, Menuhin's teacher. The album spent eighteen weeks at the top of the American classical chart and won a Grammy in 1968. It was the first time an Asian musician received one, at a time when pop groups were picking up sitar sounds.
werk/ravi-shankar-west-meets-east.listen: Listen to Prabhati and notice the interplay between the violin and the tabla. Hear how a Western violinist makes an Indian raga his own.

werk/ray-charles-genius-soul-jazz.text:
Genius + Soul = Jazz was recorded in two sessions on 26 and 27 December 1960 at Van Gelder Studio and released in 1961 on the label Impulse! Quincy Jones and Ralph Burns wrote the big band arrangements. The singer plays Hammond B3 organ on all the tracks. He was accompanied by two groups, one made up of members of the Count Basie Band and one of top players from the New York studio world.

The album reached number four in the American chart and stayed there for forty-eight weeks. The Encyclopedia of Albums singles out One Mint Julep: here the singer lets the musicians do the work while he plays the organ. In 2000 the album was voted number 360 in Colin Larkin's list of the best albums, and in 2011 it entered the Grammy Hall of Fame.
werk/ray-charles-genius-soul-jazz.listen: Listen to One Mint Julep and notice how the organ carries the songs while the band is given room to solo.

werk/ray-charles-the-genius-of-ray-charl.text:
This album was released in October 1959 on Atlantic and showed that Ray Charles wanted more than rhythm and blues. The label gave him every support with production and arrangements. The first half consists of swinging big band pieces with his own band, supplemented by players from the orchestras of Count Basie and Duke Ellington and arrangements by, among others, Quincy Jones. The second half consists of six ballads with a large string orchestra, arranged by Ralph Burns. Each side contains a tribute to Louis Jordan.

Come Rain or Come Shine, a song associated with Frank Sinatra, put his voice alone in the spotlight. Reactions differed. A reviewer in 1959 found the arrangements banal, but praised the piano playing and singled out Am I Blue? as a highlight. Later the Rolling Stone Album Guide called it perhaps the singer's most important album for Atlantic, because it announced the approach he would follow in the years to come.
werk/ray-charles-the-genius-of-ray-charl.listen: In Come Rain or Come Shine, listen to the voice: with neither strings nor band as the main focus, the attention falls mostly on the way of singing.

werk/ray-charles-what-d-i-say.text:
What'd I Say was released in late 1959 on Atlantic Records. It was really more of a compilation than a self-contained album: the songs had previously been released as singles and had not yet appeared on an album. The oldest, Roll with My Baby, dates from 1952, Jumpin' in the Mornin' from 1953. It also contains singles from 1958 and 1959.

The title track was the singer's first top ten hit. The album became his first gold record. A Billboard reviewer called it a fine, swinging album on which he is at his best. In September 1961 it entered the American album chart and reached number twenty. The critic Robert Christgau included it in his Basic Record Library of records from the fifties and sixties.
werk/ray-charles-what-d-i-say.listen: Listen to What'd I Say, his first top ten hit, and notice the energy with which Ray Charles sings the song.

werk/ray-charles-yes-indeed.text:
Ray Charles released Yes Indeed!! in 1958 on Atlantic. It was his fourth album and the second of three Atlantic LPs collecting Charles's hit singles for the label. He played piano and sang himself. The horn players included David Newman on saxophone and the trumpeters John Hunt and Marcus Belgrave.

The record contains fourteen tracks, and not a single one lasts longer than three minutes. The title track Yes Indeed!! was written by Sy Oliver, Lonely Avenue comes from Doc Pomus and most of the other songs were written by Charles himself. On a number of tracks The Raelettes and Mary Ann Fisher sing along, on others The Cookies. Marvin Israel designed the cover.
werk/ray-charles-yes-indeed.listen: Listen to Yes Indeed!! and notice how short and direct the song is: in a little over two minutes everything has been said.

werk/red-garland-the-nearness-of-you.text:
The Nearness of You is an album by the American pianist Red Garland, subtitled ballads played by Red Garland. He recorded it in 1961, and it was released in 1962 on the label Jazzland. Garland plays in a trio, with Larry Ridley on bass and Frank Gant on drums. Only in Lush Life, the piece by Billy Strayhorn, does he play entirely alone.

The repertoire consists of eight well-known songs by, among others, Hoagy Carmichael, Jerome Kern, Duke Ellington and Irving Berlin. The title thus refers to the song by Carmichael and Ned Washington, which is second on the record. AllMusic gave the album three stars and wrote that it works mainly as background music.
werk/red-garland-the-nearness-of-you.listen: Listen to Lush Life, where Garland plays alone, and notice how he lets the melody ring out without bass and drums.

werk/red-hot-chili-peppers-blood-sugar-s.text:
After Mother's Milk the band wanted to get away from producer Michael Beinhorn, and after a move from EMI to Warner Bros. they chose Rick Rubin. He suggested recording in a villa in Los Angeles where Harry Houdini was said to have lived. The members worked in that house for more than thirty days, and Anthony Kiedis recorded his vocals in his own room. The sessions were filmed for Funky Monks.

The Red Hot Chili Peppers kept their mix of punk and funk, but made more melodic songs, with less distortion and fewer metal guitar riffs. Flea deliberately played more simply and used less slap technique. Give It Away arose from a jam, and Under the Bridge began as a poem by Kiedis about a low point in his life. The record received widespread praise and made the group world famous. Guitarist John Frusciante could not cope with the fame and quit during the 1992 tour.
werk/red-hot-chili-peppers-blood-sugar-s.listen: Listen to Under the Bridge: notice how the soft, quiet guitar at the beginning changes when the whole band joins in.

werk/red-hot-chili-peppers-californicati.text:
Guitarist John Frusciante had left the group after Blood Sugar Sex Magik and had fallen into drugs. In 1998 he returned after a spell in rehab, at the urging of bassist Flea. The new songs took shape that summer in Flea's garage studio. Frusciante had to get used to playing together again and opted for a minimalist guitar style. The recording at Cello Studios in Los Angeles took just over three weeks, with Rick Rubin as producer. All four members played at the same time in the same room, with few overdubs.

The record was released on 8 June 1999 and sounds more melodic and softer than its predecessors. Alongside the familiar sexual innuendo, the lyrics deal with death, California, drugs and travel. Rolling Stone found the album more spiritual than earlier work. Otherside, the title track and Scar Tissue, which won a Grammy, became hits. It became the group's most commercially successful studio album.
werk/red-hot-chili-peppers-californicati.listen: Listen to Scar Tissue and notice the sober, restrained guitar. How much room does it leave for the vocals?

werk/red-hot-chili-peppers-freaky-styley.text:
Freaky Styley was released on 16 August 1985 on EMI America. It was the second album by the Red Hot Chili Peppers and the first studio album with Hillel Slovak, who had returned to the band after Jack Sherman was fired. After the bad experience with Andy Gill, the group was keen to work with George Clinton of Parliament and Funkadelic. Clinton agreed and first had the band spend a month with him before recording began. The record was made at United Sound Studios in Detroit, and the chemistry with Clinton was good.

The music draws on funk, punk rock and psychedelic rock, and the lyrics deal with the band members' lives in Hollywood. Jungle Man and Hollywood (Africa) were released as promotional singles, and videos were made for Catholic School Girls Rule and Jungle Man. Critics saw it as an improvement on the debut and praised the experimentation and the production. It was the last album with drummer Cliff Martinez.
werk/red-hot-chili-peppers-freaky-styley.listen: Listen to Jungle Man and notice how funk and punk meet in the rhythm of the bass and drums.

werk/red-hot-chili-peppers-the-red-hot-c.text:
This debut album was released on 10 August 1984 on EMI America and Enigma Records. Guitarist Hillel Slovak and drummer Jack Irons had left, so singer Anthony Kiedis and bassist Flea brought in Jack Sherman and Cliff Martinez. Sherman plays only on this record. The producer was Andy Gill, guitarist of Gang of Four.

The recording was uneasy. Kiedis and Flea were often at odds with Gill over the direction and found the result less raw than their 1983 demo. Kiedis was particularly hurt when he saw that Gill had written that Police Helicopter was bad. On Mommy Where's Daddy, Gwen Dickey, the singer of Rose Royce, sings along. The reviews were mixed. Even so, the record got airplay on college radio and on MTV, and it built the band's audience. Flea later said that he liked the songs but regretted the way they were recorded.
werk/red-hot-chili-peppers-the-red-hot-c.listen: Listen to Police Helicopter and notice the stuttering, angular tempo that Kiedis later described as a burst of energy.

werk/red-hot-chili-peppers-the-uplift-mo.text:
The Uplift Mofo Party Plan was released on 29 September 1987. It is the only studio album on which all four founders of the Red Hot Chili Peppers play on every track: singer Anthony Kiedis, bassist Flea, guitarist Hillel Slovak and drummer Jack Irons. Producer Michael Beinhorn urged the group to broaden its horizons. The sound is funk rock, with influences from reggae and heavy metal.

Slovak experimented with those styles and used a talk box in Funky Crime. Flea played a lot of slap bass. The record did better than its predecessors and was the group's first to enter the Billboard 200. It was also the last album with Slovak, who died of an overdose in 1988. Irons left the group afterwards.
werk/red-hot-chili-peppers-the-uplift-mo.listen: In Behind the Sun, listen to Slovak's melodic guitar line. Notice how soft and melodic it sounds next to the raw funk rock of the rest.

werk/renee-fleming-haunted-heart.text:
Haunted Heart is a jazz album on which the opera singer Renée Fleming collaborates with pianist Fred Hersch and guitarist Bill Frisell. The title song dates from 1948, written by Arthur Schwartz and Howard Dietz for the revue Inside U.S.A., where it was the biggest hit.

The repertoire is remarkably broad. Alongside jazz standards such as My One and Only Love and The Moon Is a Harsh Mistress by Jimmy Webb, there are pop songs, such as River by Joni Mitchell, My Cherie Amour by Stevie Wonder and In My Life by Lennon and McCartney. There is also classical repertoire: Mahler's Liebst Du Um Schönheit, an arrangement of Alban Berg's Wozzeck, the song Psyché by Emile Paladilhe and a piece by Heitor Villa-Lobos. The album closes with Hard Times Come Again No More by Stephen Foster.
werk/renee-fleming-haunted-heart.listen: Listen to In My Life and notice how a familiar song sounds with just piano and a singer who comes from the classical world.

werk/return-to-forever-romantic-warrior.text:
Romantic Warrior was the first album that Return to Forever recorded for Columbia Records, after four records on Polydor. In February 1976 the group retreated to Caribou Ranch near Nederland in Colorado. It was also the first record on which the credit featuring Chick Corea disappeared from beside the band's name. Some see the album as Corea's answer to a successful record by Rick Wakeman, because of its medieval themes and the influence of progressive rock.

Corea wrote the longest pieces; the other members each wrote one track. Medieval Overture sets the mood. Lenny White's Sorceress begins with a funky riff, Al Di Meola's Majestic Dance leans on rock riffs and a distorted guitar, and Stanley Clarke's The Magician is complex and playful. It became the group's most popular album, and afterwards Corea decided that the time of this line-up was over.
werk/return-to-forever-romantic-warrior.listen: Listen to Duel of the Jester and the Tyrant (Part I & II) and notice Chick Corea's intense keyboard solo.

werk/richie-havens-alarm-clock.text:
Alarm Clock was released in 1971 on Stormy Forest and is the Richie Havens album that achieved the highest chart position: number 29 on the Billboard Top 200 in the United States. He wrote most of the songs together with Mark Roth. The record opens with a live cover of Here Comes the Sun by the Beatles, which on its own reached number 16.

On the nine tracks, Paul Williams plays lead guitar, while Havens himself sings and plays guitar, and on a few songs percussion and piano. Rick Derringer plays electric guitar on To Give All Your Love Away, and Bill Shepherd wrote the string arrangement for End of the Seasons. The title track closes the record and lasts well over seven minutes.
werk/richie-havens-alarm-clock.listen: Listen to Here Comes the Sun and notice how a Beatles song acquires a character all its own here, with guitar, congas and steel guitar.

werk/richie-havens-richard-p-havens-1983.text:
This double album from 1968 combines studio recordings with live material from a concert in July 1968. It is a concept album, and it was the first time Richie Havens co-produced himself, alongside Elliott Mazer and Mark Roth. According to Mazer, he made up his own chords, which made it difficult for the many musicians. The title refers to Nineteen Eighty-Four by George Orwell: according to him there was still time, but not much.

The record mixes original work with covers, including songs by the Beatles and Bob Dylan, which he made into his own songs. The music touches on folk rock, world music and folk blues. Indian Rope Man became a well-known song, often covered and returning as African Herbsman. The album reached number 80 on the Billboard chart and received good reviews. One reviewer found it a little too long for a double album.
werk/richie-havens-richard-p-havens-1983.listen: Listen to Indian Rope Man and notice the voice and the guitar playing, which give the song its own atmosphere.

werk/richie-havens-stonehenge.text:
Stonehenge is a folk rock album from 1970 with ten tracks, most of them written by Richie Havens himself. There are also covers, such as It's All Over Now, Baby Blue by Bob Dylan and I Started a Joke by the Bee Gees. Besides guitar, the singer also played autoharp, sitar and koto, which gives the record a distinctive tone colour. Musicians such as David Bromberg on dobro, organist Warren Bernhardt and pianist Ken Lauber took part, and Bill Shepherd wrote string arrangements.

The longest track is the closing Shouldn't All the World Be Dancing, which lasts well over eight minutes. The rest of the record consists of short songs of two to four minutes, with the exception of the Dylan cover of just over five minutes.
werk/richie-havens-stonehenge.listen: Listen to It's All Over Now, Baby Blue and notice how a familiar Dylan song is sung and played here in a style of its own.

werk/rick-astley-body-en-soul.text:
Body & Soul is Rick Astley's fourth studio album and was released in 1993. Astley produced it together with Gary Stevenson, who also did the recording. Tom Lord-Alge mixed the album. Dave West on keyboards, Mark Brzezicki on drums and Nigel Hitchcock on saxophone, among others, played on it, and a choir of backing singers sang along.

The record was not a commercial success. It became his first album to miss the British album chart, although it did reach number 28 in Italy. Two singles were released: Hopelessly reached number 33 in the United Kingdom and The Ones You Love number 48. After this album Astley took a break from music for years, until his single Sleeping in 2001.
werk/rick-astley-body-en-soul.listen: Listen to Hopelessly and notice the relationship between the vocals and the keyboards beneath them.

werk/rick-astley-free.text:
Free is Rick Astley's third studio album and was released in February 1991 on RCA Records. It was the first record that was not made by the production team Stock Aitken Waterman. Astley now produced it himself, together with Gary Stevenson, and also handled the art direction of the cover. In this way he left behind the slick hit sound of his early years.

Cry for Help, a ballad, became the biggest hit from the album and reached the top ten in both the United Kingdom and the United States. Move Right Out and Never Knew Love did less well. The album reached the British top ten and the American top forty. It marked the end of four successful years for Astley.
werk/rick-astley-free.listen: Listen to Cry for Help and notice how the vocals set the tempo of the ballad.

werk/rick-astley-hold-me-in-your-arms.text:
Hold Me in Your Arms was released on 26 November 1988 on RCA and followed the successful debut. Half of the songs were written and produced by Stock Aitken Waterman. The other half consisted of his own compositions, produced by Phil Harding, Ian Curnow and Daize Washbourn. The release was delayed by several months by a fire at PWL Studios, in which part of the recorded music was lost.

The first single She Wants to Dance with Me was the first song that Rick Astley wrote himself. In the United States and Japan, Ain't Too Proud to Beg, a song by The Temptations, was also released. Critics responded in mixed ways. Music & Media saw the album as proof that he could also be a songwriter and co-producer, while AllMusic felt that, apart from the first single, it had few strong songs. It proved to be the last collaboration with the team: Astley wanted to leave the dance-oriented pop sound behind.
werk/rick-astley-hold-me-in-your-arms.listen: Listen to She Wants to Dance with Me and bear in mind that this was his first self-written single. Notice how danceable and direct the song sounds.

werk/rick-astley-never-gonna-give-you-up.text: On 27 July 1987 Never Gonna Give You Up by Rick Astley was released; he had first worked as an assistant in the Stock Aitken Waterman studio. His deep voice surprised the public: anyone hearing it expected a much older man than the 21-year-old in the video. The song reached number one in 25 countries. Twenty years later it got a second life as an internet prank: rickrolling.
werk/rick-astley-never-gonna-give-you-up.listen: Hear the tight drum machine, a Linn 9000, and the synthesizer bass that bounces merrily up and down.

werk/rick-astley-whenever-you-need-someb.text:
On 16 November 1987 RCA released Rick Astley's debut album. Most of the songs, including Never Gonna Give You Up, Together Forever and Don't Say Goodbye, were produced by the team Stock Aitken Waterman. Phil Harding and Ian Curnow worked on The Love Has Gone and Slipping Away, and Daize Washbourn on No More Looking for Love and You Move Me. In the studio, Linn drum machines and programming on a Fairlight drove the rhythms and sounds, with Mike Stock and Matt Aitken on keyboards.

The press reaction was divided. AllMusic called it an often engaging debut, while Robert Christgau wanted to advise against it. A Music Week reviewer felt that the production team set the tone of the whole. It has become Astley's best-selling album, with, according to the source, 15.2 million copies worldwide, and in 1987 it was the seventh best-selling album in the United Kingdom.
werk/rick-astley-whenever-you-need-someb.listen: Listen to Never Gonna Give You Up and notice the tight drum machine and the keyboards beneath the vocals. This is how you hear the production team setting the tone.

werk/rick-wakeman-no-earthly-connection.text:
After his world tour in late 1975, Rick Wakeman retreated in January 1976 to Hérouville in France. There he recorded a new album with his band, the English Rock Ensemble. The previous two concept albums had been expensive because of the orchestra and the choir, and A&M let it be known that this could no longer continue. He wrote much of the music during flights, inspired by a UFO that he claimed to have seen above his beach house in Miami.

It became a more serious album, without the jokes of his earlier work. He described it as partly invented, partly true: a musical autobiography about the soul, reincarnation, evolution and flying saucers. Music Reincarnate filled the whole of the first side and part of the second. The label wanted to make cuts, but he refused. The rest of side two contains The Prisoner and The Lost Cycle. The album reached number nine in England and came with a mirrored sheet for viewing the distorted cover the right way up.
werk/rick-wakeman-no-earthly-connection.listen: In The Lost Cycle, listen to how the band rounds off the storyline of this second side. The piece is about a gap in evolution.

werk/rick-wakeman-piano-vibrations.text:
Piano Vibrations was the debut of the English keyboardist Rick Wakeman, released in 1971 by Polydor. At that time he was a session musician and also played with the folk rock group Strawbs. The recording went at lightning speed: four sessions, for which he received 36 pounds in total.

It is not a record of original work. He plays covers of pop, jazz and folk on a grand piano, with the orchestra of John Schroeder and a singer who is known only as Chris. Neither his name nor that of the singer appears on the cover. The album presents a keyboardist at the start of his career, long before the great concept records that would make him famous.
werk/rick-wakeman-piano-vibrations.listen: Listen to Your Song and notice how the grand piano carries the melody while John Schroeder's orchestra plays around it.

werk/rick-wakeman-the-myths-and-legends-.text:
In the summer of 1974 Rick Wakeman lay in hospital after three mild heart attacks. A specialist advised him to stop performing, but he began writing that very evening. As a boy he had lived for five months on a farm in Cornwall, close to where, according to legend, Arthur's castle stood. That gave him the idea for a concept album about King Arthur. He sang his first ideas into a cassette recorder.

Recording took place from October 1974 to January 1975 at Morgan Studios in London, with his band, the New World Orchestra and the English Chamber Choir. The Last Battle was the first piece he wrote in hospital. The album received good reviews, although some called it an example of the excess of progressive rock. In England it reached number two. In 1975 three sold-out shows at Wembley followed, staged as an ice show.
werk/rick-wakeman-the-myths-and-legends-.listen: In Merlin the Magician, listen to the theme with which the piece begins and to how it later becomes heavier. In this way Wakeman portrayed an old man with his potions, and then the mad professor in his cellar.

werk/rick-wakeman-the-six-wives-of-henry.text:
Rick Wakeman was offered a solo record when he was playing with Yes in 1971 and had previously been with the Strawbs. He had no band, no lyrics and few ideas. During an American tour he bought a book about Henry VIII and his six wives. That is how he found the common thread: each piece is a musical portrait of one of the wives. The record is instrumental and was made in 1972 at Morgan and Trident Studios in London, with guests from Yes and the Strawbs.

He combined piano, organ, harpsichord and synthesizers, and left each musician room for their own interpretation. Anne of Cleves is free in form, and Anne Boleyn ends with a small choir singing a hymn without words. The label at first thought the record too difficult to sell. Even so, the album reached number seven in the United Kingdom in January 1973.
werk/rick-wakeman-the-six-wives-of-henry.listen: Listen to Anne Boleyn and notice the ending, where a small choir sings a wordless hymn over the piano.

werk/ricky-nelson-rick-is-21.text:
Rick Is 21 is Rick Nelson's sixth studio album and was released on 8 May 1961 on Imperial Records. It was the first record on which his first name is given as Rick; the earlier albums were released under the name Ricky Nelson.

The recording took place almost entirely at the famous United Western Recorders studios in Los Angeles, from February to April 1961. Only Do You Know What It Means to Miss New Orleans was recorded earlier, in February 1960 at Master Recorders in Hollywood. The repertoire consists of songs by, among others, Dorsey Burnette, Jerry Fuller, Gene Pitney, Johnny Rivers and Dave Burgess. Jimmie Haskell wrote the arrangements and Charles Bud Dant produced the record.
werk/ricky-nelson-rick-is-21.listen: Listen to Travelin' Man and notice how the vocals and the accompaniment together carry a song by a pop idol. Hear which instruments stand out next to the voice.

werk/rihanna-a-girl-like-me.text:
Rihanna's second album was released in April 2006, less than eight months after her debut. She worked again with Evan Rogers and Carl Sturken, and also with Stargate, J. R. Rotem and Ne-Yo, a label mate. The title fits the plan to sing in a more personal way, about things that girls of her age go through. S.O.S. was the first song to be recorded, in three days. It was originally intended for Christina Milian, who turned it down.

The album keeps the dancehall and reggae of the debut and adds ballads and a little rock. S.O.S. uses the bass line and the beat of Tainted Love by Soft Cell. Unfaithful, written by Ne-Yo, tells of a relationship falling apart, with piano and strings. Break It Off is a duet with Sean Paul. Critics felt that she gracefully avoided the second-album slump. S.O.S. became her first number one on the American chart.
werk/rihanna-a-girl-like-me.listen: Listen to S.O.S. and notice the bass line and the rhythm, which come from Tainted Love by Soft Cell. Compare that with Unfaithful, where piano and strings set the mood.

werk/rihanna-anti.text:
In 2014 Rihanna left Def Jam, which had released all her albums since 2005, and signed with Jay-Z's Roc Nation. She began recording around 2013 and was executive producer herself, with, among others, Jeff Bhasker, Boi-1da, DJ Mustard, Hit-Boy and Timbaland. She wanted an album that was soulful and timeless, not a pile of songs that would quickly wear out. The release was a long time coming and came out on 28 January 2016.

ANTI is more subdued than her earlier dance numbers, with lo-fi beats, distorted vocals and a slow tempo. The first half is bass-driven, the second minimalist and layered. It contains pop, dancehall, psychedelic soul and R&B. Work with Drake became a number 1 on the American Hot 100. Critics appreciated the emotional honesty and found the production divided, but many saw an artistic coming of age. The album received six Grammy nominations.
werk/rihanna-anti.listen: Listen to Love on the Brain and notice how the vocals go from soft to raw.

werk/rihanna-loud.text:
Loud was released on 12 November 2010 on Def Jam. It is Rihanna's fifth album and was recorded between February and August 2010, during her tour and the filming of the movie Battleship. In Los Angeles the record company deployed almost all the studios to bring writers and producers together. Some two hundred songs came out of this, of which eleven made the album. Producers included Stargate, The Runners and Alex da Kid.

After the dark Rated R she wanted to have fun again, with rousing, Caribbean-tinged dance music. California King Bed is a rock ballad and Man Down a reggae number. Only Girl (In the World), What's My Name? and S&M all reached number one in the United States. Only Girl (In the World) won a Grammy for Best Dance Recording. Critics praised the cheerful songs and her singing, although some found the record unfocused.
werk/rihanna-loud.listen: Listen to Man Down, a reggae number with an electronic rhythm, and notice how she sings with a West Indian accent.

werk/rihanna-music-of-the-sun.text:
In 2003 Rihanna was discovered in Barbados by producer Evan Rogers, who took her to New York to record demos. She did so in fits and starts, because she could only work during school holidays. Jay-Z, who had just become head of Def Jam, heard the demo with Pon de Replay and had her audition. She signed a contract that same day. The debut album was released in August 2005, produced by, among others, Rogers and Carl Sturken, Poke and Tone and Stargate.

The title refers to the Caribbean culture she comes from. The album mixes dance pop, dancehall and R&B, with guests such as Kardinal Offishall, J-Status and Vybz Kartel. Pon de Replay became a big club hit. The Last Time is a quiet song on acoustic guitar. The reviews were mixed: some praised the dancehall, others found the production somewhat generic.
werk/rihanna-music-of-the-sun.listen: Listen to Pon de Replay and notice the dancehall beat and the way she sings, with a rhythm reminiscent of reggae. Then compare that with The Last Time, which is carried mainly by guitar.

werk/rihanna-rated-r.text:
Rated R was released on 20 November 2009 on Def Jam and is Rihanna's fourth album. Recording began in March 2009 in, among other places, New York, London, Paris and Los Angeles. Her previous record, Good Girl Gone Bad, had been a great success, and after the assault by her then boyfriend in February 2009, everyone wondered whether the new songs would be about it. Producers included Chase & Status, Stargate and The-Dream. Slash plays guitar on Rockstar 101.

The sound is darker and more menacing than before: pop, hip hop and R&B with rock influences and a touch of dubstep. Rude Boy comes from dancehall and Te Amo has a Latin colouring. She sang The Last Song in the final twelve hours before the album had to be finished. Critics praised her mature performance and called the record her most layered and sensitive work.
werk/rihanna-rated-r.listen: Listen to Rude Boy and notice the dancehall influence, which sounds so different from the sombre tone of many other songs on the album.

werk/rihanna-umbrella.text: In March 2007 Umbrella by Rihanna was released, written by Terius The-Dream Nash and Christopher Tricky Stewart, with Kuk Harrell and Jay-Z. It was first offered to Britney Spears, but her record company let it go. This is how songs pass from artist to artist in the hit factory. Umbrella reached number one in many countries and became one of the best-known songs of the decade.
werk/rihanna-umbrella.listen: The post-chorus is one word in pieces: ella, ella, eh, eh. A second hook on top of the first.

werk/ringo-starr-beaucoups-of-blues.text:
Beaucoups of Blues is Ringo Starr's second studio album, released in September 1970, five months after his solo debut Sentimental Journey. It leans on country and western and is far removed from its pop-oriented predecessor. As a Beatle he had already played with country, for example with Act Naturally and Don't Pass Me By. During the recording of George Harrison's All Things Must Pass he met pedal steel guitarist Pete Drake, and together they decided to make an album.

On 25, 26 and 27 June 1970 he recorded all the songs at Music City Recorders in Nashville, with Drake as producer and local session musicians. All the songs were written especially for him. Charlie Daniels called them typical Nashville sessions: three songs in three hours. In the United States the album reached the country chart; in Britain it did not enter the charts.
werk/ringo-starr-beaucoups-of-blues.listen: Listen to I Wouldn't Have You Any Other Way, the duet with Jeannie Kendall, and notice how the two voices relate to each other.

werk/ringo-starr-goodnight-vienna.text:
Goodnight Vienna was the follow-up to Ringo, the successful album of 1973. It was recorded in Los Angeles in the summer of 1974 and released on 15 November on Apple Records. Producer Richard Perry and many of the musicians were the same as the last time, including Billy Preston, Klaus Voormann, Robbie Robertson and Harry Nilsson.

Of the other ex-Beatles, only John Lennon took part. He wrote the title track, played piano and suggested covering Only You (And You Alone) by The Platters. Elton John supplied Snookeroo, co-written with Bernie Taupin, and Nilsson gave Easy for Me. Only You was released as a single and reached number six in America. The album reached number eight there, and only number thirty in England. The reviews were generally favourable. The cover, with Ringo Starr as a space creature beside the robot Gort, is based on the film The Day the Earth Stood Still.
werk/ringo-starr-goodnight-vienna.listen: Listen to Only You (And You Alone) and notice how the singer takes over this old Platters classic, with Lennon as a guide during the sessions.

werk/ringo-starr-sentimental-journey.text:
Sentimental Journey is Ringo Starr's solo debut, released in March 1970 on Apple Records while the Beatles were falling apart. It is a collection of old pre-rock 'n' roll standards that he knew from his youth in Liverpool. He began recording in October 1969, after John Lennon had said privately that he was leaving the band. George Martin produced and each song was given a different arranger, including Paul McCartney, Klaus Voormann, Maurice Gibb, Quincy Jones and Elmer Bernstein. The cover shows him in front of a pub in the Liverpool district of Dingle.

The reactions were mixed and many Beatles fans were confused. Even so, the record reached the top ten in the United Kingdom. Later it was seen as a forerunner of standards records by, among others, Harry Nilsson and Linda Ronstadt.
werk/ringo-starr-sentimental-journey.listen: Listen to Love Is a Many Splendored Thing, on which the most studio work was spent, and notice the orchestra in Quincy Jones's arrangement.

werk/rita-reys-the-cool-voice-of-rita-re.text:
The Cool Voice of Rita Reys is the debut album of the Dutch jazz singer Rita Reys. It was released on the Dutch Philips and the American Columbia. The recordings are divided over the two sides of the LP. On one side a group led by her husband, drummer Wessel Ilcken, plays, recorded between 1955 and 1956 at the Phonogram Studios in Hilversum. On the other side a band around drummer Art Blakey plays, recorded in New York in May and June 1956, including Horace Silver and Hank Mobley.

The repertoire consists of standards, from My Funny Valentine to That Old Black Magic. Reys spent several months in the United States in 1956 and 1957 and sang there with many musicians. AllMusic calls this probably her most famous record.
werk/rita-reys-the-cool-voice-of-rita-re.listen: Listen to My Funny Valentine and notice how restrained Reys sings. Hear how little the accompaniment does to give her voice room.

werk/robert-glasper-canvas.text:
Canvas was the first album by pianist and composer Robert Glasper on a major label, Blue Note. He plays in a trio with bassist Vicente Archer and drummer Damion Reid. Saxophonist Mark Turner can be heard on two tracks, singer Bilal on two others. Almost all the songs are by the pianist himself; Riot is by Herbie Hancock. Eli Wolf was the producer.

Critics heard the tradition of Tyner, Hancock and Jarrett: rich in harmony and melody. They also heard a sound of his own in the making, with jazz lines, neo-soul turns and a touch of hip hop rhythm. JazzTimes praised above all Riot, in which a small piece of Hancock's melody serves as a five-bar loop for solos. Another reviewer found the album too uniform.
werk/robert-glasper-canvas.listen: In Riot, listen to the short melodic fragment that returns as a loop, and to what the soloists play on top of it.
